title: Insurance Claim Services Cash Application Rules for Carrier Payments
content:
**Rules.** The claim file must be in approved status when a carrier payment is recorded. Every carrier payment is recorded as the payment advice states it, including payments issued to the insured alone, and lowers the carrier receivable. A contractor direct payment can be posted to the company's jobs at once; an insured two-party check can be posted only after the insured has endorsed it, and the insured is asked to endorse within the tier's endorsement days of being notified; an insured only payment is never posted to a job, because the insured pays the company's invoices from it; a mortgagee loss draft payment stays with the mortgagee and reaches the company only as released rebuild draws. A two-party check may be endorsed only by the insured named on the claim file. A dwelling-coverage payment that can be posted is applied across the jobs of the claim file in the tier's payment allocation order: first the mitigation jobs (water, fire and mold) in order of invoiced date, earliest first, then any mitigation jobs not yet invoiced in order of opened date, and last the rebuild contract; each job takes at most its own balance due before the next job is paid. A contents-coverage payment is applied only to the contents job of the claim file. A payment remainder left after every job of the file is paid in full is not posted anywhere and is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

These Insurance Claim Services rules govern recording every carrier payment and every two-party check endorsement. The endorsement days and the allocation order are each tier's own figures.

## Route of the payment and what reaches the jobs

| Payee route on the advice | Lowers the carrier receivable | Posting to the company's jobs |
|---|---|---|
| contractor direct | yes | at once |
| insured two-party check | yes | only after the insured has endorsed it |
| insured only | yes | never; the insured pays the company's invoices from it |
| mortgagee loss draft | yes | stays with the mortgagee; reaches the company only as released rebuild draws |

## Evidence

- File status: the claim file's status on the system record must be approved when the payment is recorded.
- Endorsement: the endorsing person must be the insured named on the claim file, checked against the claim file's customer and the check's payee route on the system record.

## Allocation of a postable dwelling payment (hypothetical figures)

A dwelling payment of 9100.00 on a file whose water job (invoiced 3 March) owes 4000.00, whose fire job (invoiced 10 March) owes 3500.00, whose mold job (not invoiced) owes 2600.00 and whose rebuild contract owes 6000.00: the water job takes 4000.00, the fire job 3500.00, the mold job 1600.00, and the rebuild contract nothing. Had the payment been 18000.00, the four would take 4000.00, 3500.00, 2600.00 and 6000.00, and the remaining 1900.00 would be posted nowhere and handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

A contents-coverage payment goes only to the file's contents job.
